newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Wednesday in lacklustre trade, dealers said.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. March housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation data.
Housing starts for March are forecast to be around 1.46 million annualised units compared with 1.528 million units reported in February.
March industrial production is expected to rise to 0.6 percent against February's 0.5 percent.
Capacity utilisation for March is expected to rise to 83.6 percent from 83.3 percent in February.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. The market is now waiting for tonight's release of the housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation figures, for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact here," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday eased 1/8 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Thursday/Friday eased 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent but week-fixed was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and six-months unchanged at 6 5-7/8 percent.
